Hi Samir —

Thanks — answering each question inline below. High level: Redwood supports per-tenant region pinning with configurable failover behavior. Here are the specifics we typically provide to financial customers: 

1) Region isolation / failover
- For pinned tenants we place compute and persistent stores (model KV cache snapshots and customer-managed storage keys where applicable) in the selected region. In steady-state, inference traffic is served from that region and will not egress to other regions.
- Failover modes:
  • Manual failover — customer triggers failover to a designated secondary region (recommended when you need full control).
  • Automatic failover — optional; we offer async cross-region failover. In automatic mode, requests will start routing to the secondary region when health checks fail in primary. Note: automatic failover can result in data crossing regions during the incident window.

2) Retention & PII
- Default: non-PII telemetry (aggregated metrics) retained per account defaults to 90 days; request/response token logs and full audit trails default to 30 days.
- Zero-retention option: for PII-sensitive streams we support a ‘no-log’ ingest pipeline (redact-on-ingest + no persistent token logs) that ensures no request/response tokens are retained beyond ephemeral processing. This is available as a configuration on a per-tenant basis and is commonly requested by regulated customers.
- Token-level logs used for quality/debugging are opt-in and can be scoped to internal debug-only roles; we provide role-based access controls for those artifacts.

3) Backups & RTO/RPO
- Backups are encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys (KMS) where required. We store backups in the primary region by default; cross-region encrypted backups are an opt-in configuration for active-active or cold DR workflows.
- Typical backup retention is configurable (default 30 days). For DR we offer two models:
  • Warm standby (asynchronous replication of model artifacts + snapshots): lower RTO (minutes to an hour depending on model size) but costs more.
  • Cold restore from cross-region backups: higher RTO (hours) but lower cost.

4) Audit logs / SIEM integration
- We provide downloadable tenant-scoped audit logs (JSON/NDJSON) and a streaming integration to common SIEMs (Splunk, Datadog, Sumo Logic). Logs include request metadata, timestamps, routing decisions, and admin actions (no full PII unless you’ve opted into token retention).

Notes / recommended defaults for AcmeBank
- If you need strict in-region guarantees for certain BUs, recommend per-tenant pinning + manual failover mode.
- For PII-heavy flows, enable the no-log pipeline for those endpoints and use KMS-managed keys for backups.
